items.title: Claude Opus 5.5 launches, 20% cheaper than Opus 5
items.summary: Claude Opus 5.5 matches Fable 5.1 performance at $4/$20 per million input/output tokens, 20% less than Opus 5, with cache reads down 60% to $0.20. It hits 66.4% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 81.8% on OSWorld 2.0, and 67.7% on Humanity's Last Exam with tools. Available now on Claude.ai, AWS, GCP, and Azure. (2 minute read)

items.title: OpenAI ships GPT-6 Sol and Luna
items.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and Luna split frontier capability and cost into two everyday-work models, already the top story on HN with 1,634 points and 784 comments. Both are live now, letting teams pick between the two cost/capability tradeoffs directly. (2 minute read)

items.title: Pentagon ties AI overreliance to Iran school strike
items.summary: The Pentagon says overreliance on AI contributed to a missile strike on a school in Iran, according to Bloomberg's investigation. (3 minute read)

items.title: The economics of running open-weight models
items.summary: A new analysis lays out the cost structure behind serving open-weight models yourself versus paying for hosted inference. (2 minute read)

items.title: Claude finds a new CRISPR-like enzyme system
items.summary: Running 950 agents for 21 hours and 210M tokens, Claude screened 200,000+ reverse transcriptases down to 20 candidates and spotted a new pattern: a CRISPR-like array of non-coding repeats and an unknown accessory protein alongside a known reverse transcriptase. The function is still unconfirmed, but Anthropic published it as a preprint for further wet-lab work. (3 minute read)

items.title: Hackers claim they breached the FBI
items.summary: A hacking group claims to have stolen data on all FBI employees, according to 404 Media. (2 minute read)

items.title: Where open-weight models stand right now
items.summary: Interconnects lays out the current competitive landscape among open-weight model releases. (2 minute read)

items.title: Splitting quantization across prefill and decode
items.summary: A new paper proposes quantizing LLM prefill and decode stages separately instead of applying one scheme to both. (3 minute read)
